verdict.rationale: Phaser ships extensive first-party docs across core concepts (scenes, physics, loader, animations, TypeScript definitions) which would give an LLM many patterns to draw from, but community comments concretely contradict the 'well-documented, stable API' premise: users call the docs 'the worst I've seen' and note the main site was 'outdated by about 4 major releases,' and TypeScript support is described as only a 'best-effort' DefinitelyTyped layer rather than native. These are specific documented complaints, not vague skepticism, directly undermining the claim that APIs are stable/well-documented enough for reliable first-try LLM code generation. missing for 10: independent evidence of actual LLM code-gen success rates on Phaser, confirmation that docs complaints are resolved/current, and native (not best-effort) TypeScript support.
